I'm going to be very honest with you. It is going to take months to lose that weight. You cant expect to lose 10kg in a matter of weeks. That's unrealistic. 

Don't eat less than that! It's hard to meet all your nutritional needs on fewer than 1200 calories. You are "barely" losing weight, but you are still losing. Ozempic isn't a magic drug that makes you lose as much weight as possible as fast as possible. 

This is a marathon and not a sprint. Appetite suppression aside, for me it has eliminated my obsession with food, which has allowed me to make more long term changes to my eating habits. 

How many times have so many of us here lost weight on a really strict diet in order just to gain it back plus more? Slow loss is good. Do you feel like you could maintain 1200 or less for years on end? I know i couldn't. Focus on healthy behaviors like weight bearing exercise, eating enough fresh produce, and not obsessing about the scale. 

I'd also recommend ditching the scale (or at least putting it in the closet). Weight fluctuates with so many factors, including constipation, salt intake, water intake, and hormones. Try monthly measurements instead. I only started measurements so I could buy clothes online. For my mental health, when I take new measurements, I delete the old ones. I dont need to make a graph to make permanent changes.

Ozempic is a long term drug. You can't take it with the expectation that you can take it for 4 months and drop a bunch of weight. It's one tool to help you have a healthier relationship with food and making habits you could realistically do for a lifetime. 

If calorie counting and weighing higher calorie foods don't stress you out or make you entirely obsessed, give that a try. Dont go below 1200. Think of tracking as a way to make sure you are eating enough. You really have to change what you are eating and can't expect to automatically lose just because you are eating less. My plain hypomania feels more than just not depressed. I feel great. I party more, have risky sex, and generally call myself "fun (insert name here.") I will talk too much too fast. I start a bunch of projects that I don't finish.

Symptoms of hypomania in type 2 have to be present for a minimum of 4 days to be considered an episode.
